chunks: My father (Muhammad ibn al-Hasan) narrated to us, pleased with him, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi narrated from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Tufayl, from Ali (peace be upon him).

He said: 'No Muslim servant says: There is no god but Allah, except that [the words] ascend, breaking through every roof, passing through nothing of his sins except that they obliterate them, until they reach an equal amount of good deeds, and then they stop.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (the core declaration of faith)

ai.seo_question: How does the declaration of monotheism erase sins according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes the metaphysical ascent of the declaration of monotheism, which pierces the layers of the heavens to reach the Divine Presence. This spiritual journey actively neutralizes the believer's sins, a concept reflecting the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of *Tawhid* as both a verbal affirmation and a cosmic force that elevates the soul. The process culminates in the balance of good deeds, underscoring the interplay between faith and divine mercy in the afterlife.
